source.title: Finding Features Causally Upstream of Refusal
source.authors: Daniel Lee; Eric Breck; Andy Arditi

record.tranche_reason: The study obtains a difference-in-means refusal direction using the cited method and directly adds that direction to prompts that otherwise receive compliance, reporting refusal outputs. It does not test the direction's removal.
record.gate_note: The study also steers upstream SAE latents and reports outputs; those interventions are recorded as findings about upstream features, not as tests of the claimed single direction. Gradient rankings and latent selections are omitted because they are used to select features for steering.
record.test_reason: Mainly the study uses the Arditi et al. difference-in-means direction as a tool: a gradient target and projection metric for finding upstream SAE features. It also reports its own direct test of V1's addition half. Adding that direction (Gemma-2-2b-it, layer 15 resid_post, final-token diff-in-means, coefficient 30, prompt positions only) turns compliance into refusal on three prompts (Tables 2, 4, 6). This is the original method and measure, so T1, but only qualitative and for induction.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Gradients of the refusal-direction projection with respect to layer-5 activations surface interpretable, prompt-relevant SAE features that are causally upstream of refusal. Steering them induces refusals reflecting the steered concept. The authors frame this as preliminary and limited to cherry-picked borderline prompts.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the difference-in-means direction from layer 15 resid_post at the final prompt position, but reports direct addition only, not ablation across every layer and position or a capability assessment.
record.method_sensitivity: The study uses hand-crafted prompts near the refusal/compliance border and chooses layer 5 arbitrarily; a comment notes sensitivity to phrasing. The apocalypse latent is steered at 1.5 times maximum activation rather than the usual factor of 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering top refusal-gradient-aligned layer-5 SAE latents induces refusals whose stated reasons match the latent's concept, on three borderline prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Upstream concept features that reframe a prompt as harmful feed the refusal direction and can trigger feature-consistent refusals.

fits_no_version.finding: For the hugging prompt, top latents (and the refusal gradient) raise the refusal projection more than 10 random latents, peaking near coefficients 10-30.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-selected upstream latents move the refusal-direction projection more than random latents.

record.problems: The study tests one model with three hand-crafted borderline prompts. The authors say the prompts are not representative of randomly selected prompts and note that layer choice was arbitrary and results may be phrasing-sensitive. Direct refusal-direction steering is shown qualitatively; no ablation or general-capability test is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Ablation removing refusal on harmful prompts. Retention of other abilities. Refusal induction on a broad or random set of harmless prompts. Only three hand-picked borderline prompts are used, with no rates.
Positive- and negative-gradient latents read as harmful vs harmless interpretations, but harm judgment is not separated from the refusal decision.

missing.what: Steering by the refusal gradient itself versus refusal projection

record.verdict_notes: The study mostly assumes V1 and builds on it. Andy Arditi, first author of the original source, co-wrote this post, but the post is not itself an original source, so a verdict is given. In comments he calls the prompts very cherry-picked and phrasing-sensitive. The V1 support is weak: qualitative, one model, three prompts, induction only. Reviewers could reasonably reclassify the study as T4.

versions.untested_parts: Does not ablate the direction, test removal of refusal, assess other abilities, or establish the effect on a broader set of harmless requests. Direct steering's precise intervention layer and positions are not stated.
Jailbreak suppression of the direction and training against its ablation.
Whether refusal is affine, conical, or involves multiple directions.
Separate encoding of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Effects of refusal training method or timing.

relationships.condition: Gemma-2-2b-it, three hand-crafted borderline prompts that are complied with unsteered; addition of the diff-in-means direction at coefficient 30 on prompt tokens
relationships.reason: Adding the direction produces refusals on all three prompts (D1, D2, D3). The evidence is qualitative single generations on cherry-picked borderline prompts.
relationships.display_finding: Adding the direction produced refusals on all three selected borderline prompts that received compliant responses without steering.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
